title: Add benchmark-lab adaptive-batching reporting pipeline v110
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: consolidate adaptive-batching profiling and reporting into a single repeatable pipeline (v110) that produces baselines for latency/throughput and drives continuous regression detection. This PR adds the DAG for the reporting pipeline, representative workload runners optimized for mixed and low-latency scenarios, new profiling baselines for adaptive batching heuristics, and telemetry exporters to push results to the benchmark-lab reporting cluster. Changes are intentionally incremental so downstream dashboards and alerts can be validated before we switch production consumers.

What changed (high level):
- New pipeline: benchmark-lab/pipelines/adaptive_batching_v110/dag.py (orchestrates workloads, profiles, and report upload).
- Representative runners: benchmark-lab/runners/mixed_workload_runner.py and benchmark-lab/runners/low_latency_runner.py (concrete configs for model size, batch shapes, sequence lengths, and concurrency sweeps).
- Profiling baselines: benchmark-lab/baselines/adaptive_batching/v110/*.yaml (baseline metadata + perf thresholds).
- Telemetry: benchmark-lab/exporters/bench_reporter.py (uploads JSON summaries, metrics tags for variant/model/hw) and updated Prometheus metric names to follow benchlab.v2 namespace.
- CI: added an end-to-end bench job that runs a minimal DAG against a small synthetic dataset to catch regressions.

Checklist: [x] pipeline dag implemented and unit tested locally, [x] representative runners validated against local GPU CI, [x] baselines included, [x] exporters conform to report schema, [x] documentation added (README + quickstart).

Testing and validation: Unit tests for new modules added under benchmark-lab/tests (fast). End-to-end bench CI runs a tiny representative workload in CI (containerized) — flaky integration encountered on first run (GPU allocation timeout) and was rerun; final CI state is passing. Metrics emitted were spot-checked in staging and matched expected distributions.

Rollout plan: Merge to main, deploy reporting DAG to bench-lab staging for 48h, validate reports/dashboards for regressions, then flip a feature flag to start feeding production dashboards. Backout plan: disable DAG from the scheduler and revert the exporters if malformed reports are observed.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps model-specific tuning out of the baseline YAMLs; follow-up PR will add automated threshold-calibration using historical runs. See linked Linear tasks for follow-ups.
